public_rationale: For 2024, the year he was writing in, the two leading standalone generative AI companies lost far more than they made. CNBC confirmed that OpenAI expected about $5 billion in 2024 losses on $3.7 billion in revenue. Anthropic's IPO filing shows 2024 revenue of $386 million against a $2.98 billion operating loss, about 7.7 times revenue. So the money part of the claim holds. The second part, that the technology had not solved enough complex problems to justify its costs, is partly opinion. It is read here as revenue not covering costs, which these figures also show. Anthropic's operating profit in 2026 comes long after the period described and does not change the 2024 picture.
limitations: The OpenAI figures are company projections reported by the press, not audited results.
Anthropic's 2024 operating loss comes from a secondary summary of the S-1, because the SEC page could not be read.
'Generative AI' is read as the model makers. Suppliers such as Nvidia were profitable.
The 'complex problems' clause is graded only in economic terms.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI loses far more money than it makes and has not yet solved complex problems that would justify its costs.

statement.excerpt: generative AI loses so much more money than it makes and has yet to solve the complex problems to justify its costs

from_speaker: "generative AI loses so much more money than it makes"
"has yet to solve the complex problems to justify its costs"
present tense, as of the post (2024-08-12)
our_interpretation: "Generative AI" is read, in the post's context, as the business of building and selling large language models and products built on them. The leading standalone model makers (OpenAI, Anthropic) are the clearest measure, because the big tech firms do not break out generative AI profit. Chip suppliers such as Nvidia are not the generative AI business itself.
"Loses so much more money than it makes" is read plainly: the leading model makers' losses were large compared with their revenue. Losses bigger than revenue clearly meet it.

He names no period. The claim describes an ongoing state at the post date, so the period is calendar 2024, the year in progress. Reports before the post projected 2024 losses, and full-year 2024 figures were reported later.

"Has yet to solve the complex problems to justify its costs" is partly a value judgment. It is read here in economic terms: as of 2024, what customers paid for generative AI did not cover what it cost to provide. This clause is not graded as a separate technical claim.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports or filings show that leading generative AI model makers had 2024 losses large compared with their revenue (for example, losses equal to or above revenue), so revenue did not cover costs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible reports or filings show that leading generative AI model makers were profitable in 2024, or had small losses compared with revenue.
